claims.text: Toughness is retained when a continuous, ductile, disordered matrix contains brittle intermetallic phases only as isolated inclusions.
Increasing the volume fraction and connectivity of a brittle phase beyond a critical threshold causes it to form a continuous network.
A continuous brittle-phase network promotes crack propagation and loss of toughness.
The proposed initial state is a refractory high-entropy alloy with a predominantly disordered BCC matrix and approximately 3–4 vol% discrete brittle intermetallic precipitates.
Increasing Cr content can promote formation of a brittle intermetallic phase in a refractory high-entropy alloy.
Changing heat treatment can alter whether ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases are continuous, discrete, or weakly ordered.
Vacuum arc melting with repeated remelting can be used to improve chemical homogeneity.
Brittle-phase connectivity relative to a continuous disordered BCC matrix is the structural variable governing toughness.
A continuous ductile matrix deflects or blunts propagating cracks.
Isolated brittle precipitates act as local barriers to crack propagation.
Once the brittle phase percolates, it becomes a preferential path for crack propagation.
An isolated brittle-phase distribution should produce greater strain to failure and lower crack-propagation rates than a continuous brittle-phase distribution.
Formation of a continuous brittle phase should significantly reduce fracture toughness relative to the baseline, even if strength increases.
The baseline with a continuous disordered BCC matrix and approximately 3–4 vol% isolated intermetallic precipitates has a balanced combination of strength and toughness.
The proposed connectivity mechanism should apply to refractory high-entropy alloys under near-equilibrium processing at room to moderately high temperatures.
The hypothesis may not apply after rapid quenching or severe irradiation because these conditions introduce additional defect or phase-formation mechanisms.
The critical connectivity threshold is not quantitatively established and may vary among alloy systems and processing routes.
Solid-solution hardening and other strengthening mechanisms may modulate the observed toughness response.

A lack of toughness loss after a confirmed isolated-to-continuous brittle-phase transition, or a toughness improvement despite increased connectivity, would falsify the proposed governing relationship.
